utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Buena Park' by name among the cities in its service area. Buena Park's own OCPA page also confirms SCE handles transmission, distribution, metering, and billing.

value.name: Orange County Power Authority (OCPA) - Smart Choice (default)
value.notes: Confirmed directly via the City of Buena Park's own page: 'New customer accounts will be automatically enrolled at Smart Choice' as the default 2026 energy plan. Buena Park is a founding OCPA member city. Customers may switch plans or opt out to SCE generation at any time without fees.

county.notes: Buena Park is a well-documented Orange County city; also listed under Orange County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

permit_authority.value: City of Buena Park Building Division

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Buena Park/Orange County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Completed Eligibility Checklist for Expedited Solar Voltaic Permitting (job address, permit number, and initialed general/electrical/structural/fire-safety items)
Solar PV Plan and supporting documentation
Roof layout diagram showing all panels, modules, clear access pathways, and approximate locations of electrical disconnects and roof access points
Valid contractor's license and business license (verified automatically by Symbium)

value: The permit plans and Eligibility Checklist must be on the job site at time of inspection

The inspector conducts a plan review and inspection of the system, comparing it to the checklist — any deviation requires new plans to be submitted for review under the standard (non-expedited) process

timeline_days.notes: The city's page describes Symbium as providing 'no wait time for City review' for eligible expedited submissions, but does not state a specific number of days for the standard review pathway.

value.program_or_pathway: Symbium automated instant permitting (expedited, systems 10kW AC or less) / standard review process (non-qualifying systems)
other_conditions: Roof-mounted on a one- or two-family dwelling or accessory structure
Panel/module arrays cannot exceed the maximum legal building height
System must be utility-interactive and without battery storage to qualify for the expedited pathway

Electrical requirements: no more than 4 PV strings per MPPT input with source-circuit fusing in the inverter (2 without), no more than 2 inverters for central-inverter systems, single-phase AC service panel of 120/220 Vac with a bus bar rating of 225A or less, connected to the load side of utility distribution equipment
Fire safety requirements: clear access pathways, fire classification, required markings/labels, and a roof layout diagram

permit_fees.notes: Permit fees are paid directly through the Symbium platform, but no dollar amount is stated on the city's page.
